source_refs.excerpt: public static final Supplier<AngelheartVialItem> ANGELHEART_VIAL = ITEMS.register("angelheart_vial", AngelheartVialItem::new);
public static final Supplier<PhoenixDownItem> PHOENIX_DOWN = ITEMS.register("phoenix_down", PhoenixDownItem::new);

rows.concrete_observation: Native registered Angelheart and Phoenix items register LOW death handlers into TreeSet; CommonEventHandler beforePlayerDeath accepts only Player, selects first canApply&&apply true, breaks then cancels event. Eligibility is item existence across provider inventory handlers, not holding in hand, fixed health threshold or a stored resurrection cooldown. Phoenix replaces first matching whole inventory slot with one AngelicFeather using void swap helper; Vial gets first actual matching ItemStack then shrink1. Both apply always return true after their work without resource-mutation success receipt or checking positive recovered health. Phoenix sets maxHealth*configured percentage, optionally removes a fixed list of vanilla negative effects, adds source-equality lava/drown bonuses and configurable resistance/regen ignoring effect admission, then sends particles. Vial consumes, sends particles and glass-break sound BEFORE assigning recovered health/removing effects. Thus evidence cue is within tentative handler, before outer final cancel, not an engine death-settlement acknowledgement. Comparator returns1 for equal priority (even self), so do not claim deterministic same-priority rescue winner or standards-correct order. Default provider prepends newly added handlers, main/offhand/armor backed accessors are explicit; extensions may precede these. Registered S2C payloads carry only fixed Vec3. Receiver requires local player then spawns401 vanilla flame particles for Phoenix, or8 item particles plus100 effect attempts for Vial at supplied coordinates. It never resolves victim UUID/entity/generation, does not track target motion and has no packet throttle; native particle lifetime/render mechanics not examined.
rows.application_to_boss_immune: For truthful Boss refusal feedback, distinguish death rescue from damage immunity and emit result semantics at a verified decision boundary. Inventory mutation, health assignment, status admission and outer event cancellation are separate outcomes. Coordinate-only replay is a snapshot, not target anchoring; do not infer target-safe receipt or actual survival from displayed particles or glass sound. This is research, no resurrection feature added.
rows.semantic_dedup: One proposed inventory-backed native death-rescue family, Phoenix/Vial variants and their different FX merged. Generic first-match handler infrastructure, inventory wrappers, particle loop counts, source constants and negative-effect names0. Existing reliquary hunger conversion hurt defenses are not repeated; the death event/resource replacement and feedback-before-cancel chain is separate for Russell to assess. Compare other accepted rescue chains: no teleported rescue destination, owner familiar life budget, persisted down state or finite shield hit threshold. No automatic credit for another item name; helper0.
rows.limitations: Static current upstream NeoForge code, not a1.20.1 port. No proof configured health percentage positive, actual revival succeeds, inventory extension transactional semantics, all listeners honor cancellation, payload delivery ordering, vanilla flame lifetime/depth or visible sound/particles. Comparator issue is source observation, no runtime fault reproduced. No per-target immune text or Boss implementation. Neither game nor production code executed.
